content.text:
I have surveyed every candidate location and all detection phrases. Findings:

- **§2.1 (p0013)**: "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies… its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall."
- **§12.3 (p0051)**: express negation — Customer free to engage any supplier; no exclusivity commitment.
- **§12.4 (p0052)**: a restriction on *Vendor* (won't compete with our analytics products) — benefits us, not flagged.
- Every "exclusive" hit elsewhere is a non-exclusive licence grant (§13.1), remedies language (§19.3, §21, §30.2), or forum selection (§28.2) — none bind Customer to buy from Vendor.

No redline is warranted; the document sits at the preferred position.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer, so the rule sits at the preferred position and no redline is needed. Section 12.3 goes further than mere silence: it expressly confirms that nothing restricts Customer from engaging any supplier and that Customer has made no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment. Section 2.1 reinforces this commercially, stating that "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies" and that Customer's decision not to enter another Order Form "is not a breach or shortfall". Searches for the full range of detection phrases ("sole supplier", "sole and exclusive provider", "all of its requirements", "shall not procure ... from any third party", "preferred/primary supplier", "right of first refusal") returned nothing binding Customer, and the candidate sections flagged by the planner (sec-2, sec-4, sec-7, sec-12) contain no requirements or sole-source language. The remaining "exclusive" references are unrelated: a non-exclusive licence grant to Customer (§13.1), exclusive-remedy carve-outs (§19.3, §21.5, §30.2), and exclusive jurisdiction (§28.2). Section 12.4, which bars Vendor from marketing a service competing with Customer's proprietary analytics products, is an exclusivity-style restriction running in our favour and is expressly not a deviation under this rule; we retain it. Because the preferred checklist is met, the fallback limitations (defined product category, 12-month cap, automatic termination on service-level or delivery-date failure) are not engaged.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
mappings.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
